Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 14, verses 1–5:

Explanation of the words:

Alif-Lam-Ra: This is one of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah). It is written الۤر and read alif-lam-ra. Leaving its meaning to God (al-tafwid) is safer, and it is the saying that God alone knows what He intends by it.

Kitab: That is, this is a great Book.

Anzalnahu ilayka: O Muhammad (ﷺ).

Min al-zulumat: That is, from the darkness of disbelief to the light of faith.

Al-'Aziz al-Hamid: That is, the One praised for His bounties.

'An sabil Allah: That is, Islam.

'Iwajan: That is, crooked.

Bi-ayatina: That is, the nine miracles: the staff, the hand, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the obliteration (of crops), and the years of drought and the shortage of fruits.

Wa-dhakkirhum bi-ayyam Allah: That is, with His trials and His blessings.

The meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾ God alone knows what He intends by them. And His words: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you﴾ That is, this is a Book of great worth, which We have sent down to you, O Our Messenger, so that you may bring mankind out of the darkness, that is, the darkness of disbelief and ignorance, into the light of faith and sacred knowledge. This is ﴿by the permission of their Lord﴾, that is, by His guidance and help, ﴿to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, that is, to the way of the Mighty, the Overpowering, the Praiseworthy, who is praised for His bounties and graces upon His servants and all His creation. ﴿God, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ in creation, dominion, disposal and management. This is God, the owner of the path that leads to human felicity and perfection. The disbelievers turn away from it, and indeed they bar others from it, so woe to them because of a severe punishment. The disbelievers are ﴿those who prefer the life of this world﴾, that is, they prefer the present life, so they work for this world and leave work for the Hereafter, because they do not believe in it. ﴿And they bar﴾ themselves and others as well ﴿from the path of God﴾, that is, Islam. ﴿And they seek to make it crooked﴾, that is, crooked. They want Islam to conform to their desires and whims, so that they might accept it and be content with it as a religion. The Exalted said: ﴿Those are in far-off error﴾. By this conduct, which is manifested in preferring this world over the Hereafter, barring from Islam, and attempting to subordinate Islam to achieve their greeds and lusts, they are in a far-off error from which the one in it cannot return to guidance.

His words in verse [4] of this context: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people﴾, that is, in their tongue by which they speak and understand one another, for the wisdom that he might make things clear to them. Then God leads astray whom He wills to lead astray, according to His sunnah in misguidance, and guides whom He wills in the same way. ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, the Overpowering who is not resisted in anything He wills, ﴿the Wise﴾, who places everything in its proper place. Therefore He does not lead astray except one who desires misguidance, seeks it, chooses it and prefers it, and who opposes guidance and wars against the guided and those who call to guidance. It is not part of His wisdom to lead astray one who seeks guidance, strives towards it, adheres to its path, loves it and loves its people.

His words: ﴿And We had already sent Moses﴾, that is, Moses, the prophet of the Children of Israel, ﴿with Our signs﴾, that is, with Our proofs and evidences indicating his prophethood and guiding to what he called to. They were nine signs, among them the hand and the staff. ﴿That bring your people out of the darkness into the light﴾, that is, bring your people out of the darkness of polytheism into the light of monotheism. ﴿And remind them of the days of God﴾, that is, We said to him: remind them of the days of God, which are His trials and His blessings, when He saved them from the punishment of the people of Pharaoh and bestowed upon them such favours as the manna and the quails. This was so that they would be moved to thank God by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger. His words: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful person﴾, that is, indeed in that reminder of trials and blessings are proofs by which one may infer God's bounty and grace which calls for gratitude. But those who find those proofs in the reminder are the people of patience and gratitude, indeed they are the many of patience and gratitude. As for others, they see in it neither proof nor sign.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The establishment of proof against those who deny the Noble Qur'an, for it is composed of disjointed letters such as Alif-Lam-Ra, Ta-Sin-Mim, Alif-Lam-Mim and Ha-Mim, and they were unable to produce its like, or even a single surah like it.

2. Clarification that disbelief is darkness and faith is light.

3. Clarification of the wisdom in God, Exalted, sending the messengers in the languages of their peoples.

4. Affirmation that it is God who creates guidance, while the servant has no more than acquisition (kasb).

5. The virtue of reminding of good and evil, so that one may thank God and be mindful of Him.

6. The virtue of patience and gratitude.

**Explanation of the words:**

*"And when Moses said"*: meaning, remember when Moses said.

*"They subjected you to"* (yasumuna-kum): meaning, they made you taste.

*"And they spared your women"* (wa-yastahyuna nisa'akum): meaning, they let them live.

*"A great trial from your Lord"* (bala' min rabbikum 'azim): meaning, a test and an examination, which may be either good or evil.

*"And when your Lord proclaimed"* (wa-idh ta'adhdhana rabbukum): meaning, your Lord made known.

*"With clear proofs"* (bil-bayyinat): meaning, with clear arguments for the truth of their call to prophethood, to the oneness of God, and to the Resurrection in the Hereafter.

*"They put their hands to their mouths"* (fa-radda aydiyahum fi afwahihim): meaning, the nations put their hands to their mouths, that is, they gestured to them to be silent.

*"Disquieting"* (murib): meaning, causing doubt (rayb).

**Meaning of the verses:**

*"And when Moses said to his people"*: meaning, remember, O our Messenger, when Moses said to his people, the Children of Israel, *"Remember the favour of God upon you"*: that is, so that you may give thanks for it by affirming His oneness and obeying Him. Whoever remembers, gives thanks. He made clear to them the kind of favour: their deliverance from Pharaoh and his chiefs, who used to torment them through oppression and enslavement. So he said: *"They subjected you to the terrible torment"*: meaning, they made you taste evil torment, the worst and most severe of it. *"And they slaughtered your sons"*: meaning, the newborn infants, because the soothsayers or political advisers told Pharaoh: "It is not unlikely that your throne will fall and your rule will end at the hands of a man from the Children of Israel." **Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 14, verses 10–14:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Afi Allahi shakk* (أفي الله شك): That is, there is no doubt about the existence of God or about His Oneness, since the interrogative is one of denial.

*Ila ajalin musamma* (إلى أجل مسمى): That is, until the appointed term of death.

*Bi-sultanin mubin* (بسلطان مبين): With a clear proof that demonstrates the truth of your claim.

*Yamunnu ala man yasha'* (يمن على من يشاء): That is, He bestows prophethood and messengership upon whomever He wills for it.

*Wa qad hadana subulana* (وقد هدانا سبلنا): That is, the ways by which we came to know Him, and by which we came to know the greatness of His power and the might of His dominion.

*Li-nukhrijannakum min ardina* (لنخرجنكم من أرضنا): That is, from our homelands, or that you return to our religion.

*Li-man khafa maqami* (لمن خاف مقامي): That is, his standing before Me on the Day of Resurrection for reckoning and recompense.

**The meanings of the verses:**

The context continues with what Moses reminded his people of, in His words: ﴿Has there not reached you the news of those before you: the people of Noah...﴾ [Ibrahim: 9]. Then His words, ﴿Their messengers said﴾, that is, the messengers said to those disbelieving nations: ﴿Is there doubt about God?﴾ That is, how can there be doubt concerning the Oneness of God, when He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth? The Creator of the heavens and the earth alone cannot reasonably have a partner in worship; there is no god but Him. And His words, ﴿He calls you﴾ to faith and righteous deeds free of polytheism, ﴿that He may forgive you of your sins﴾, which is every sin between you and your Lord, both major and minor sins; as for the wrongs done to people, return them to their owners. ﴿And defer you to an appointed term﴾, that is, He postpones the punishment from you so that you die at your decreed appointed times.

And His words, ﴿They said﴾, that is, the disbelieving nations said to their messengers: ﴿You are not but human beings like us﴾, that is, you are nothing but humans like us, ﴿you wish to turn us away﴾, that is, to divert us, ﴿from what our fathers used to worship﴾, namely their gods, that is, their idols and images which they claim are deities. And their saying: ﴿So bring us a clear authority.﴾ The disbelievers said to the messengers: bring us a clear authority, that is, a manifest proof that shows the truth of your claim that you are God's messengers to us. The messengers answered, saying what God related of them in His words: ﴿Their messengers said to them, "We are only human beings like you"﴾, that is, we are nothing but humans like you; what you are unable to do, we are equally unable to do. ﴿But God bestows His favor upon whom He wills﴾, that is, except that God bestows His favor upon whomever He wills with prophethood; He has bestowed it upon us. So we inform you of what our Lord, your Lord, has commanded us to inform you of, as we command you and call you, not on our own initiative but by what He has commanded us to command you and call you to. ﴿It was not for us to bring you an authority except by the permission of God﴾, that is, by His will and power; He is the One of unlimited will and the power that nothing can frustrate. Therefore we rely upon Him alone, and upon Him ﴿let the believers rely﴾, for He suffices them for all that concerns them.

Then the messengers said, admonishing their peoples with what has preceded: ﴿And why should we not rely upon God, when He has guided us to our ways?﴾, that is, to the paths by which we came to know Him and came to know His greatness and the might of His dominion. What, then, would prevent us from relying upon Him, when He is the Mighty, the Strong? ﴿And we will surely bear with patience what you inflict upon us﴾ with your tongues and your hands, relying upon God until God avenges us upon you. ﴿And upon God let those who rely [truly] rely﴾, for He is the Guarantor of everyone who trusts in Him and entrusts his affair to Him, relying upon Him alone to the exclusion of anything else.

And His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely expel you from our land, or you must return to our religion."﴾ This is a report from Him, Exalted is He, of what the disbelieving nations said to their messengers. They said, threatening them with exile and banishment from the lands for everyone who turns away from their religion and worships other than their gods: ﴿We will surely expel you from our land or you will return to our religion﴾, that is, our religion to which we adhere. Then God revealed to His messengers what He related: ﴿So their Lord revealed to them: "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers, and We will surely settle you in the land after them."﴾ He said "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers" and did not say "We will surely destroy them," indicating the cause of destruction, which is wrongdoing, namely polytheism and corruption, so that this be an admonition to the worlds.

And His words, Exalted is He: ﴿That﴾, that is, the deliverance of the believers and the destruction of the wrongdoers, is a recompense ﴿for those who fear My standing [before Me]﴾, that is, standing before Me on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and fear My threat﴾, conveyed through the tongues of My messengers, of punishment for whoever disbelieves in Me, associates others in My worship, and dies without repenting to Me from his disbelief, his polytheism, and his wrongdoing.

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The falsity of doubt about God's existence, His knowledge, His power, His wisdom, and the obligation to worship Him alone, because of the abundance of evidence, the strength of proofs, and the clarity of demonstrations.

2- An explanation of what the people of disbelief used to confront the messengers of God and those who call to Him, Glorified and Exalted is He, and what the messengers used to reply to them with.

3- The obligation to rely upon God, Exalted is He, and the invalidity of relying upon anyone else, since there is no sufficient protector but God.

4- The obligation to be patient with harm endured in the way of God and to await relief through the seizing of the wrongdoers.

5- The consequence of wrongdoing, which is ruin and destruction, does not change or fail to come to pass, however long the time may be.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 14, verses 15–20:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-istaftahu (and they sought victory): i.e., the messengers sought a victory (fath) for themselves, meaning triumph over their wrongdoing peoples.

Wa-khāba (and failed): i.e., lost and perished.

Kullu jabbārin ʿanīd (every obstinate tyrant): i.e., every wrongdoer who compels people to his will, stubbornly persistent in defiance.

Min māʾin ṣadīd (from putrid water): i.e., it is what flows as a liquid from the bodies of the people of the Fire, mixed with pus, blood and sweat.

Yatajarraʿuhu wa-lā yakādu yusīghuhu (he gulps it down, yet hardly able to swallow it): i.e., he swallows it mouthful after mouthful because of its bitterness, and he almost cannot get it down because of its foulness and bitterness.

Wa-yaʾtīhi al-mawtu min kulli makān (death comes to him from every place): i.e., because of the intensity of the punishment surrounding him, all the causes of death are present, yet he does not die.

Aʿmāluhum ka-rmād (their deeds are like ashes): i.e., their righteous deeds, such as maintaining family ties, kindness to parents, hospitality to guests and freeing captives, and their corrupt deeds, such as worshipping idols by sacrificing to them, making vows, swearing oaths and devoting themselves around them, are like ashes.

Lā yaqdirūna mimmā kasabū ʿalā shayʾ (they gain nothing of what they earned): i.e., they obtain no reward from their deeds, however small, because they are void through polytheism.

Wa-mā dhālika ʿalā Allāhi bi-ʿazīz (and that is not difficult for God): i.e., it is not hard or impossible for Him.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the end of the account of what Moses mentioned to his people about the histories of the nations before the Children of Israel. God, the Exalted, says in reporting about them: ﴿And they sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant failed﴾, meaning: the messengers sought victory, that is, they asked God to grant them triumph over His enemies and theirs, and God answered them. ﴿And every obstinate tyrant failed﴾, meaning: every oppressive, rebellious wrongdoer who opposes the truth and its people lost and perished. And His saying: ﴿Before him is Hell﴾, meaning: Hell lies ahead of him, awaiting him; he will enter it after his destruction, and he will be thirsty and seek water, and the guardians will give him drink ﴿of putrid water﴾, meaning: it is the discharge of the people of the Fire, which is pus, blood and sweat. ﴿He gulps it down﴾, meaning: he swallows it mouthful after mouthful because of its bitterness. ﴿Yet he can hardly swallow it﴾, meaning: it enters his burning inner body, parched with thirst, but he almost cannot swallow it because of its foulness, stench and bitterness and heat. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Death comes to him from every place, but he is not dead﴾, meaning: this obstinate tyrant, who is in Hell and whom thirst kills, and who is given the putrid water, death comes to him because its causes exist and are abundant from every place, since the punishment surrounds him from above him, below him, from his right and from his left; yet he is not dead, because God, the Exalted, has not willed that. God says: ﴿He will neither die therein nor live﴾ [al-A'la: 13], and He says: ﴿It will not be decreed for them so that they would die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾ [Fatir: 36]. And beyond that punishment in which he is, there is ﴿a punishment﴾, meaning another kind of punishment, ﴿severe﴾, meaning intense and unbearable.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The example of those who disbelieved in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes on which the wind blows violently on a stormy day﴾, meaning: a day on which the wind blows fiercely. ﴿They gain nothing from what they earned﴾, meaning: from deeds in the world, ﴿of any reward or good result from them﴾. This is the likeness of their righteous deeds, such as various kinds of good and kindness, and of their evil deeds, such as polytheism, disbelief, and worship of other than God, which they hoped would benefit them. All of it goes away like ashes carried off and scattered by the wind, blown violently on a fierce, stormy day.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is the far-reaching error﴾, meaning: that which the parable indicates is the far-reaching error for whoever falls into it, since all his deeds have gone to waste without any gain, so he benefits from none of them and becomes among the losers.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen that God created the heavens and the earth with truth?﴾, meaning: Do you not know, O Messenger, that God created the heavens and the earth with truth, that is, for the sake of humankind, so that they would remember God and give Him thanks? If a person disowns his Lord, disbelieves in Him, and associates others with Him in worship, He punishes him with the painful punishment described earlier in this context, because God did not create the heavens and the earth in vain or falsehood. Rather, He created them and what is in them so that He would be remembered and thanked therein. Whoever abandons remembrance and gratitude, He punishes with the most severe and enduring punishment. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If He wills, He will take you away﴾, O people who rebel against His obedience and associate others with Him, ﴿and bring a new creation﴾ other than you, who worship Him and affirm His oneness. ﴿And that is not difficult for God﴾, meaning: it is not impossible or unattainable, because God is capable of all things.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The fulfilment of God's promise to His messengers in His saying: ﴿So their Lord revealed to them: "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers"﴾ [Ibrahim: 13], and what follows.

2- The general failure and loss of the people of polytheism, disbelief and wrongdoing.

3- The greatness and severity of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

4- The invalidity of the deeds of polytheists and disbelievers, and their failure in them, since they gain nothing from any of them.

5- The punishment of the people of disbelief, polytheism and wrongdoing is inevitable, because they did not remember and did not give thanks, and remembrance and gratitude are the purpose of all existence; when they trifled with life, they deserved an everlasting punishment.

﴿And they will come forth before Allah all together﴾: that is, all creation will come forth before Allah, and that is on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Indeed, we were to you followers﴾: that is, we followed you in what you believed and did.

﴿So can you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?﴾: that is, can you ward off from us some of the punishment?

﴿Is there for us any means of escape?﴾: that is, any refuge, way of flight, or deliverance.

﴿When the matter has been decided﴾: by bringing the people of Paradise into Paradise and the people of the Fire into the Fire.

﴿I cannot help you﴾: that is, I cannot rescue you from what you are suffering of punishment and distress.

﴿Beneath which rivers flow﴾: that is, beneath its palaces and trees flow the four rivers: of water, milk, wine, and honey.

Meaning of the verses:

In these verses is a swift presentation of the scene and what follows it, the settling of the people of the Fire in the Fire and the people of Paradise in Paradise, establishing the principle of revelation, monotheism, and the Last Resurrection with irrefutable proofs. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they will come forth before Allah all together﴾, that is, mankind will emerge from their graves, believers and disbelievers, righteous and corrupt. ﴿And the weak will say to those who were arrogant﴾, that is, the followers, to the leaders and directors of people by virtue of the power and authority they had. ﴿Indeed, we were to you followers﴾, that is, followers of you in your beliefs and in what you practiced, ﴿So can you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?﴾, that is, can you lift from us some of the punishment by virtue of our following you? So they answered them with what Allah the Exalted related about them: ﴿Had Allah guided us, we would have guided you﴾. They now acknowledge that guidance is in the hand of Allah and affirm this, but we went astray and so led you astray. ﴿It is all the same for us whether we show anxiety or are patient; there is for us no means of escape﴾, that is, no way out of this punishment and no refuge. Here Satan stands up to speak among them, as Allah the Exalted related with His words: ﴿And Satan will say﴾, that is, Iblis, the enemy of the children of Adam, ﴿when the matter has been decided﴾, by the people of Paradise being brought into Paradise and the people of the Fire being brought into the Fire: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you a promise of truth﴾, that whoever believed and did righteous deeds, keeping away from polytheism and sins, He would admit to His Paradise and honor in His proximity; and that whoever disbelieved, associated partners, and disobeyed, He would admit to the Fire and punish with the torment of humiliation in the abode of destruction. ﴿And I promised you﴾, that the promise and threat of Allah were not true nor realized, ﴿but I broke it to you﴾ in what I promised you, and in that I was lying to you, deceiving you. ﴿And I had no authority over you﴾, that is, no material force by which I compelled you to follow me, nor any supernatural influence by which I forced you to accept my call, ﴿except that I invited you, and you responded to me﴾, that is, but I invited you, ﴿so you responded to me.﴾ Therefore, ﴿do not blame me, but blame yourselves. And ﴿indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment﴾, that is, for the polytheists is a painful, agonizing punishment. And the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted﴾, that is, Allah admits those who believed, that is, affirmed Allah and His Messenger and what His Messenger brought, ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, which are the acts of worship by which Allah made His servants devout, legislating them in His Book and upon the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ, ﴿into gardens﴾, orchards, ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾, that is, through its palaces and trees flow rivers of water, milk, wine, and honey, ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, not leaving them nor desiring any change from them. And His saying: ﴿their greeting therein will be, "Peace"﴾, that is, Peace be upon you, their Lord greets them, the angels greet them, and they greet one another with peace; it is a word of supplication for safety from every defect and disturbance, and a greeting seeking everlasting life.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that imitation and following do not serve as an excuse for their practitioner before Allah the Exalted.

2- Clarification that Satan is the one worshipped besides Allah the Exalted, since it is he who called to the worship of other than Allah and beautified it for people.

3- Affirmation of Allah's knowledge of what has not yet occurred: how can the dialogue in the verses, which had not yet taken place, be known? Yet it is in Allah's knowledge as it will be, and it will occur exactly as the verses describe, without a single letter of it failing.

4- Warning to the wrongdoers of a painful punishment.

5- Deeds admit one to Paradise only as a cause and no more; otherwise, entry into Paradise is by the permission and pleasure of Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 14, verses 24–30:

Explanation of the words:

"A good word" (kalimah tayyibah): it is "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah" (ﷺ).

"Like a good tree" (kashajarah tayyibah): it is the date palm.

"A bad word" (kalimah khabithah): it is the word of disbelief (kufr).

"Like a bad tree" (kashajarah khabithah): it is the bitter colocynth (hanzal).

"Uprooted" (ujtuttat): i.e., it was pulled up from its trunk (juththah), meaning its body and its essence.

"With the firm word" (bil-qawl ath-thabit): it is "There is no god but Allah."

"And in the Hereafter": i.e., in the grave, where the two angels ask him about what they ask: they ask him about his Lord, his religion and his Prophet.

"They exchanged the blessing of Allah for disbelief" (baddalu ni'mata Allahi kufran): i.e., they exchanged monotheism (tawhid) and Islam for denial and polytheism (shirk).

"The abode of ruin" (dar al-bawar): i.e., Hell (Jahannam).

"And they set up rivals to Allah" (wa ja'alu lillahi andadan): i.e., equals (shuraka').

Meaning of the verses:

The verses establish monotheism, resurrection and recompense. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not considered, O Messenger,﴾ i.e., have you not known ﴿how Allah has presented an example: a good word﴾ which is the word of faith that the believer says ﴿like a good tree﴾ which is the date palm ﴿whose root is firmly fixed﴾ in the earth ﴿and whose branches are in the sky﴾, ﴿giving its fruit﴾ i.e., giving its food, that is its fruit which is eaten from it at all times: unripe, half-ripe, ripened, fresh dates and dried dates, in the morning and in the evening ﴿by the permission of its Lord﴾ i.e., by His power and subjection. Thus the word of faith, "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," yields for the servant righteous deeds at all times; it is in his heart, and the righteous deeds that proceed from it are raised up to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah presents examples for the people that perhaps they will be mindful﴾ i.e., just as this example was presented for the believer and the disbeliever in this context, He presents examples for people, believers and disbelievers alike, perhaps they will be mindful, i.e., in hope that they will remember, take admonition, believe and do righteous deeds, and thus be saved from the punishment of Allah.

His saying: ﴿And the example of an evil word﴾ is the word of disbelief in the heart of the disbeliever ﴿like an evil tree﴾ which is the bitter colocynth, bitter and with no good in it, and it has no firm root and no branch in the sky ﴿uprooted from the surface of the earth; it has no stability﴾ i.e., it has no permanence, and it bears only what is in it of bitterness, bad taste and lack of blessing.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ This is a promise from Allah, may He be exalted, to His sincere believing servants that He will keep them firm in faith whatever trials and tribulations there may be, until they die in faith. ﴿And in the Hereafter﴾ i.e., in the grave, for it is the threshold of the Hereafter, when the two angels ask them about Allah, about the religion and about the Prophet: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?" Then He keeps them firm with the firm word, which is faith, and its essence is "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and the righteous deed which is Islam.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah leads astray the wrongdoers﴾ is the counterpart of the guidance of the believers: He does not grant them success in the firm word until they die in disbelief, and so they perish and lose, because of their insistence on polytheism, their calling others to it, and their oppression of the believers and harming them on account of their faith.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah does what He wills﴾ affirms His free will. He, the Mighty and Majestic, keeps firm whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, and there is no objection to Him and no denial, with the knowledge that He guides and leads astray by a lofty wisdom that makes His guidance and His leading astray both mercy and justice.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not considered﴾ i.e., has it not reached your knowledge, O Messenger, ﴿those who exchanged the blessing of Allah﴾ which is Islam that the Messenger of Allah brought them, with its guidance and goodness, so they denied the Messenger of Allah, denied what he brought, and were content with disbelief, and by that they brought down their people, who urged them to disbelief and encouraged them to deny, they brought them down ﴿to the abode of ruin﴾. Those among them who perished at Badr as disbelievers went to Hell. The abode of ruin is Hell, where they will burn, i.e., be scorched by its heat and flames ﴿and wretched is the settlement﴾, i.e., the place of residence to which they brought their people. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they set up rivals to Allah in order to lead [others] astray from His way﴾ i.e., those who exchanged the blessing of Allah for disbelief, who were the disbelievers of Makkah, set up rivals to Allah, i.e., equals, whom they worshipped: al-Lat, al-Uzza, Hubal, Manat and other false gods. They set up these rivals and called to their worship, in order to lead astray and to lead others astray from the way of Allah, which is Islam, the path leading to the pleasure of Allah, may He be exalted, and His noble proximity. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "Enjoy yourselves﴾ i.e., with what you have of the enjoyments of the life of this world ﴿for indeed, your destination is the Fire﴾ i.e., the end of your affair is ﴿to the Fire,﴾ where you will arrive after your death if you persist in polytheism and disbelief until you die upon it.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Approval of striking examples to bring meanings closer to minds.

2- A comparison between faith and disbelief, and the word of monotheism and the word of disbelief, and the good or evil that each of these categories yields.

3- Good news to the believer that Allah will keep him firm in his faith until he dies a believer, and of salvation from the punishment of the grave, where he answers Munkar and Nakir correctly, through Allah's keeping him firm.

4- The imperative in His saying, may He be exalted, "Enjoy yourselves" is neither for permission nor for obligation, but for threat and warning.

His saying: ﴿And the example of an evil word﴾ is the word of disbelief in the heart of the disbeliever ﴿like an evil tree﴾ which is the bitter colocynth, bitter and with no good in it, and it has no firm root and no branch in the sky ﴿uprooted from the surface of the earth; it has no stability﴾ i.e., it has no permanence, and it bears only what is in it of bitterness, bad taste and lack of blessing.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Approval of striking examples to bring meanings closer to minds.

2- A comparison between faith and disbelief, and the word of monotheism and the word of disbelief, and the good or evil that each of these categories yields.

3- Good news to the believer that Allah will keep him firm in his faith until he dies a believer, and of salvation from the punishment of the grave, where he answers Munkar and Nakir correctly, through Allah's keeping him firm.

4- The imperative in His saying, may He be exalted, "Enjoy yourselves" is neither for permission nor for obligation, but for threat and warning.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 14, verses 31–34:

Explanation of the words:

﻿"لا بيع فيه ولا خلال" (There is no trading in it, nor friendship): This is the Day of Resurrection, on which there is no trading, no ransom, and no close friend (khullah) who benefits, nor any friendship.

Al-Fulk (the ships): That is, the ships. The word fulk indicates a plural, and it may be masculine or feminine.

Da'ibayn (ceaselessly): Moving in their orbits, never slackening, until the end of the worldly life.

La-zalumun kaffar (truly wrongdoing and ungrateful): Greatly wrongdoing toward himself and others, and greatly disbelieving. This describes him so long as he does not believe and become guided; if he believes and is guided, this description is removed from him.

The meaning of the verses:

When Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger to say to those who exchanged the blessing of Allah for disbelief, ﴿Say: "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾ [Ibrahim: 30], He also commanded His Messenger to say to the believers: establish the prayer and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and openly, so that by this they may ward off the punishment of the Day of Resurrection with which the disbelievers were threatened. So He said: ﴿Tell My servants who have believed to establish the prayer﴾, that is, to perform it in the manner in which it was legislated: completing its bowing and prostration, performing it at its appointed times, in congregation, and in complete purity, facing the qiblah, so that it bears fruit for them in the purification of their souls and the cleansing of their spirits. ﴿And spend﴾ and continue spending at all times ﴿secretly and openly﴾, ﴿before there comes a Day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿on which there is no trading nor friendship﴾: no buying, by which a person could obtain what he might ransom himself with, nor any friendship that benefits him, nor intercession except by the permission of Allah the Exalted.

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, brought them into existence and began their creation, ﴿and sent down water from the sky﴾, which is rainwater, ﴿and brought forth thereby fruits﴾ and grains ﴿as provision for you﴾, by which you live and your lives are sustained. ﴿And He subjected to you the ships﴾, that is, the ships, ﴿to sail through the sea by His command﴾, that is, by His permission and subjection, carrying on them merchandise and goods from region to region, and riding them likewise. ﴿And He subjected to you the rivers﴾ flowing with sweet waters, so that you may drink and irrigate your farms and fields. ﴿And He subjected to you the sun and the moon, both constant﴾, never slackening in their motion and their movement through their mansions, for your benefits which are not accomplished except by the light and heat of the sun and the light of the moon and its movement through its stations. ﴿And He subjected to you the night and the day﴾: the night for you to rest in and be at ease, and the day for you to work in and earn your livelihoods. ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾, of what you are in need of for the sustenance of your lives. This is Allah, who deserves your worship, out of desire for Him and fear of Him. This is the true God who must be worshipped alone, without partner, and not those idols and images that you worship and call others to worship, to the point that it has led you to disbelief, obstinacy, and even wrongdoing, evil and corruption.

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾, that is, after He enumerated many of His blessings, He informed that it is impossible for a human being to count the blessings of Allah upon him or to enumerate them in any way whatsoever. And He established a truth at the end of this admonition and reminder, which is that when a human being is deprived of faith and divine guidance, ﴿he is indeed a wrongdoer﴾, that is, greatly wrongdoing, greatly ungrateful, and great in disbelief, and we seek refuge in Allah the Exalted from that.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The obligation of establishing the prayer, paying zakat, and increasing charity to ward off the punishment of the Fire.

2. The permissibility of open charity as well as secret charity, although the latter is better.

3. Acquaintance with Allah the Exalted, for knowledge of Allah is what bears the fear of Him.

4. The obligation to worship Allah the Exalted and the invalidity of worshipping other than Him.

5. The description of the human being with wrongdoing and disbelief, and the severity of these, so long as he does not believe and remain upright upon the path of Islam.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 14, verses 35–41:

Explanation of the words:

﴿هَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدَ آمِنًا﴾ (this city secure): i.e., make Makkah a city of security, where everyone who enters it is safe.

﴿وَٱجْنُبْنِي﴾ (keep me away): i.e., put me far away.

﴿أَن نَّعْبُدَ ٱلْأَصْنَامَ﴾ (from worshipping idols): i.e., keep us away from worshipping idols.

﴿أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ (they have led many people astray): i.e., by people's worship of them.

﴿مَن تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّي﴾ (whoever follows me is of me): i.e., whoever follows me in monotheism is among the people of my religion and faith.

﴿مِن ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾ (of my offspring): i.e., some of my offspring, namely Isma'il (peace be upon him) and his mother Hajar.

﴿بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ﴾ (in a valley without cultivation): i.e., Makkah, for there were no farms in it or around it at that time.

﴿تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ (incline towards them): i.e., yearn for them and incline towards them, out of desire for the Hajj and 'Umrah.

﴿عَلَى ٱلْكِبَرِ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ﴾ (in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq): i.e., despite his old age, for he was ninety-nine years old at that time, and Ishaq was born to him when he was one hundred and twelve years old.

﴿وَلِوَٰلِدَىَّ﴾ (and my parents): this was said before it became known to him that his father had died upon polytheism.

﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلْحِسَابُ﴾ (the day the reckoning takes place): i.e., the day people stand for the reckoning.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to establish monotheism, prophethood, resurrection and recompense, and these verses contain that. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِۧمُ﴾ (And when Ibrahim said), means: recall when Ibrahim said. How could one recount what Allah had not revealed to him? This explains the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the descent of revelation to him. His saying, ﴿رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدَ ءَامِنًا﴾ (My Lord, make this city secure), means: possessing security, so that whoever enters it is safe for his self and his wealth. By "the city" is meant Makkah.

His saying, ﴿وَٱجْنُبْنِي وَبَنِيَّ أَن نَّعْبُدَ ٱلْأَصْنَامَ﴾ (And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols), contains an affirmation of monotheism, which is the worship of Allah alone. The meaning of "keep me away" is: put me, my children and my grandchildren far away. Allah answered him, and none of his offspring or their offspring was a polytheist. His saying, ﴿رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ (My Lord, they have led many people astray), is the reason for his request to his Lord that He keep him and his sons from worshipping them. The leading astray of people came about through their worship of them, so they went astray in the valleys of polytheism. His saying, ﴿فَمَن تَبِعَنِي﴾ (Whoever follows me), i.e., of my offspring, ﴿فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّي﴾ (then he is of me), i.e., upon my religion and faith. ﴿وَمَنْ عَصَانِي﴾ (And whoever disobeys me), i.e., does not follow me in the religion of Islam: if You punish him, that is Your right, and if You forgive him and do not punish him, ﴿فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾ (indeed You are Forgiving, Merciful).

His saying, ﴿رَّبَّنَآ إِنِّىٓ أَسْكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾ (Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring), i.e., some of my offspring, namely Isma'il, with his mother Hajar, ﴿بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ﴾ (in a valley without cultivation), which is Makkah, for there was no cultivation in it or around it at that time, nor for long distances and many ages thereafter. ﴿عِندَ بَيْتِكَ ٱلْمُحَرَّمِ﴾ (by Your Sacred House): he said this by knowledge from Allah that there would be a House for him in this valley. The meaning of "sacred" is "forbidden," and Allah has made it sacred, so Makkah is sacred until the Day of Resurrection: its game may not be hunted, its grass may not be cut, blood may not be shed in it, and fighting in it is not permitted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 14, verses 42–46:

Explanation of the words:

﻿"Of what the wrongdoers do": i.e., the polytheists of Makkah and others.
